notes.title: Demo Out Now!
notes.content:
[h2]The Oceaneers Demo is Now Available! Read about the demo, and more on languages below.[/h2][p][/p][p][b]As developers we want the game to be a fun experience with good value. Features in the game are subject to change and your feedback can effect this. It's important to know the parts you enjoy as much as the parts you don't, so please make a post in the forum and let us know![/b] [/p][p][/p][h3]How You Can Support The Game[/h3][olist][*][p]Wishlist it.[/p][/*][*][p]Let your favorite YouTuber/Streamer know about the game.[/p][/*][/olist][p][/p][h3]What To Expect[/h3][list][*][p][b]Important: If it's shown in the objectives, you CAN do it in the demo![/b][/p][/*][*][p]A "speed run" of the demo (bare minimum to reach the end) is around 1.5 hours. Some players have already spent 4-20+ hours in the demo by researching and building everything available.[/p][/*][*][p]The game is part survival-crafting, part colony-sim. If you like either of those genres there is a good chance you will enjoy this (players that don't play many colony-sims have enjoyed Oceaneers due to the direct control over characters).[/p][/*][*][p]The demo is what we consider the "Normal" difficulty of the game. In the full game you will have control over various aspects, including whether characters can perish or leave your group.[/p][/*][*][p]The demo allows you to play the first part of the story, which progresses through important mechanics such as expeditions and resurfacing islands.[/p][/*][*][p]You will get to see a large part of the research tree and even research a good number of buildings in the demo (if it doesn't have a demo lock you CAN research it). The full game research tree will include even more than what is shown.[/p][/*][*][p]You can recruit one additional survivor in the demo, unlike the full game which will have many more.[/p][/*][*][p]You can send expeditions to a few sectors. The full game takes place in the entire region and beyond into other regions.[/p][/*][*][p]Overall, the demo lets you experience what the gameplay feels like. The full game has much more content and features you would expect from this type of game (farming, fishing rods, smelting etc), as well as plenty of features you don't typically see in this type of game (bunkers, story progression etc).[/p][p][/p][/*][/list][h3]More Languages[/h3][p]We are planning to add more languages further into development. The game text is still evolving and we made the decision to keep it English only for now to allow us to focus on faster development and updates. In addition to this, the game has a pretty quirky and sometimes comedic tone (with the occasional pop culture reference), which adds some challenge to localization.[/p][p][b]You can show us if you are interested in a language by:[/b][/p][olist][*][p]Wishlisting the game (we see wishlists per region)[/p][/*][*][p]Let us know via forums/discord.[/p][/*][/olist][p]The number of wishlists and interest shown for each region heavily influences the languages we will localize into.[/p][p][/p][h3]Controller & Steam Deck Support[/h3][p]Some players have already played on the Steam Deck, but we don't have official support just yet. We do plan to have it fully playable on the Steam Deck further into development.[/p][p][/p][p]Controller support is challenging for this type of game that has this much depth, and we don't want the gameplay to be limited by controller inputs. Our plan is to look into this once we have all of our features in to see what is possible. We have good experience implementing controllers and it is on our mind during development, but we are also aware of the limitations.[/p][p][/p][h3]Found a Bug?[/h3][p]Please report them! Whether it's a typo or something more significant please let us know via the forums or via Discord.[/p][p][/p][h3]Help & Guides[/h3][p]This genre of game naturally comes with a lot of freedom, and this includes freedom to make mistakes (e.g. not building water production for your colony). Figuring things out is a big part of the fun for these types of games![/p][p]Having said that, if you struggle to survive you can follow the progression guide shown on the side of the screen and there is a bunch of tutorials in the handbook.[/p][p][/p][h3]If Somethings Needs Better Tutorials[/h3][p]There is a lot of depth in the game and we already have a heap of tutorials shown in the handbook. We do have more tutorials planned so if you find something is not explained well enough or are still confused about anything, be sure to let us know.[/p][p][/p][h3]"What game is it like"[/h3][p]We like to ask players what game it reminds them of, and, "oh buoy", we have seen just about every game under the sun mentioned by now! [/p][p]It's been really interesting to see what type of games players have brought up - obviously this depends a lot on which games payers have played in the past. In no particular order:[/p][list][*][p]Don't Starve and Paper Mario (in relation to the art style).[/p][/*][*][p]Oxygen Not Included, Rimworld, The Survivalist, Cult of the Lamb.[/p][/*][*][p]Raft (and open world survival crafting games in general).[/p][/*][*][p]The Flame in The Flood, Flotsam, Frostpunk & Sheltered.[/p][/*][*][p]A hint of Fallout/Fallout Shelter.[/p][/*][*][p]Monkey Island, The Sims, Craft the World, Clanfolk.[/p][/*][/list][p]We knew there would be comparisons to similar looking games (like Don't Starve and Oxygen Not Included), so we were extremely pleased to see players add comments to this comparison that [b]Oceaneers is still very different and innovative[/b], it's very much doing its own thing.[/p][p][/p][h3][b]What's Next!?[/b][/h3][p]We are hard at work on the full game! Recently we have been improving crop farming, fishing rods and smelting metals - then tying all of the survival progression into the story/objective progression.[/p][p][/p][h3][b]Come have a chat![/b][/h3][p]Our community is growing, and everyone has been amazing and really friendly. Come chat with the devs and other players in our [url="https://discord.gg/4Xz6qNpwH5"]Discord[/url][/p][p][/p][h2]Leaving Feedback[/h2][p]If you encounter any bugs, or would love to discuss features please do so via the Steam forums or our Discord. It's really helpful to know about the parts of the game you enjoy, as well as anything you don't.[/p][p][/p][p]You can also check discord for a list of known bugs, community suggestions and upcoming plans![/p][p][/p][p]
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------


[/p][h3]⚡ Be sure to Wishlist Oceaneers, and stay tuned for the next dev diary and more announcements. ❤️[/h3][p]

[/p][h3]Join Us![/h3][p]Join our discord to discuss the game and share your ideas!

notes.title: Playtest Extended! Patch 0.0.4M Now Live
notes.content:
[p]Thanks so much for everyone that has joined the playtest and provided feedback, it's going so well that we are going to extend it for a few more days! Lots of players are really enjoying the experience, in particular the unique twists and story that opens up near the end of the build.[/p][p]Also.. people seems to [b]really[/b] enjoy kicking seagulls 😂[/p][p][/p][p]We have also just dropped a new patch to improve the new player experience, and we have even more plans for this as we go.[/p][p][/p][h2]Patch 0.0.4M[/h2][list][*][p]The handbook guide has been overhauled and now allows you to play (and replay) tutorials on various topics, and includes a handy search function.[/p][/*][*][p]You can now equip tools from the selected character box without opening the character sheet.[/p][/*][*][p]The character list no longer shows need stats, and instead shows the character occupation (we have more planned for this in the future).[/p][/*][*][p]Relaxing at a fire now recovers energy slowly (previously it only stopped energy from decreasing). Note that this is not intended to replace beds. This is significantly slower that sleeping in a bed during the day, and much slower than sleeping in a bed at night.[/p][/*][*][p]Automated relaxing was previously based on whether mood was low, now it will also take into account whether energy is low.[/p][/*][*][p]Replaced some music tracks that may have youtube content ID flags.[/p][/*][*][p]Seagulls can now steal waste from large waste piles and tiny waste pile pickups (what a shame….)[/p][/*][*][p]Characters now have Relax on the lowest priority, so they will prefer any other tasks, and wont interrupt tasks to go and relax.[/p][/*][*][p]Characters that relax at a fire (automatically) will interrupt it to go do a job if there is one available, unless you manually gave them the relax command.[/p][/*][*][p]Events now also show in the center of the screen so you can quickly notice them, they disappear quickly but stay longer in the event list on the right hand side.[/p][/*][*][p]Increased Waste Bin storage amount from 15 to 30 (this is a temporary change for the demo since it doesn’t have other ways to deal with waste).[/p][/*][*][p]Moved the handbook button to make it stand out more.[/p][/*][*][p]Added a menu button to the top of the interface.[/p][/*][*][p]Added a tutorial about accessing the tutorials…[/p][/*][*][p]The new day summary will now show some quick tips, which include very short tips about things you may have missed along the way.[/p][/*][*][p]The new day summary includes a reminder to check the character sheet to find out why your characters are losing resolve.[/p][/*][*][p]Added a note to the workpost about enabling jobs in character sheets, and added requires workpost to the relative area in the character sheet.[/p][/*][*][p]Added a Help button to the escape menu, which takes you to the tutorials in the handbook.[/p][/*][*][p]Added a note about water barrels in the Food Crate & Provisions dialogs.[/p][/*][*][p]Added a description to the science boost dialog.[/p][/*][*][p]When starting a new game with the Default or Cozy survivor group, you now start with a coconut shell.[/p][/*][*][p]Opening escape menu or handbook should now cancel any current building placement action[/p][/*][*][p]Pressing the character sheet keybind (default C) will now select a character and open the sheet if no character was selected.[/p][/*][*][p]Changes to the research tree to make the categories more obvious.[/p][/*][*][p]Replaced the colony island guide with a tutorial popup.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed the character sheet missing the dark background blockout.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed a bug where there was a tiny chance the keypad could spawn on an island crumble.[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][p][/p][p][/p][h3][b]Oceaneers Steam Playtest Continues![/b][/h3][p]Sign up directly from our Steam Page if you are interested in taking part in the playtest.[/p][p][/p][h3]Visit the Oceaneers Steam page and click the "Request Access" button![/h3][h3]

notes.title: Playtest Patch 0.0.4J Now Live
notes.content:
[p]Thanks to everyone providing feedback on the playtest so far, looks like everyone is having a lot of fun which is great to see! There are still a few more days left on the playtest![/p][p][/p][p]We wanted to put up a patch that focuses on some improved raft controls, so here it is. Love to you hear your thoughts on the changes. More improvements to come![/p][p][/p][h2]Patch 0.0.4J[/h2][list][*][p]Raft movement changes. Right clicking with a raft selected now shows the context menu by default, you can hold CTRL just to do a move without the menu. [/p][list][*][p]You can use the Work in Area command on the ocean for characters on or near the raft to automatically do tasks in the raft work area. Some people did discover this feature previously, it has been improved and the delay before characters look for things to do has been reduced.[/p][/*][*][p]The raft mast can be selected to change the size of the work area. We have removed the previous work area settings for the raft only for now, and this function works regardless of whether characters have automation enabled. This was needed to simplify the process and avoid confusion, we may add back some filters later.[/p][/*][*][p]You can queue up Work Areas, characters automatically board, drive and work.[/p][/*][*][p]You can still manually move the raft, select characters and fully micromanage them as you desire (sometimes you just want to harvest one item).[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p]When you give a character the “Drive Raft” command, the raft will automatically be selected (unless you are holding SHIFT to queue commands)[/p][/*][*][p]Most debris piles that gave beachwood now give +1 beachwood.[/p][/*][*][p]Added a “Pickup Items” category to automation workposts. Spoiled waste will only be picked up if you have the storage for it.[/p][/*][*][p]Automating salvaging will now include Science Cubes, Science Capsules and Bottles in the work area.[/p][/*][*][p]Resource tooltips now show growth conditions for plant seeds.[/p][/*][*][p]Renamed “Progression Guide” heading to “Starter Guide”[/p][/*][*][p]“Open handbook” is no longer a pre-requisite of other objectives, but it still shows as an objective.[/p][/*][*][p]Added a link to the feedback form when quitting the game.[/p][/*][*][p]Added “Build a bed” to the Starter Guide objectives.[/p][/*][*][p]Added new BioSoil recipe to the composter, this is now the base recipe, with fertilizer recipes to come later from higher tier resources.[/p][/*][*][p]Added a note to dead things like crabs, to show they need to be butchered to get the resources used in food etc.[/p][/*][*][p]Added a note about rain to the dirty water pool.[/p][/*][*][p]Added a note about more survivors to the Survivor Stories new game screen.[/p][/*][*][p]The “Explore the island” Story objective has been made more specific to “Read the strange note”.[/p][/*][*][p]Added “Send an expedition” to the Story objectives, to indicate that it is necessary to progress the story.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed some typos on tools.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed characters trying to automatically relax at a fire that was already full of people relaxing.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed characters sometimes facing the wrong way when kicking nodes.[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][h3][b]Oceaneers Steam Playtest Continues![/b][/h3][p]Sign up directly from our Steam Page if you are interested in taking part in the playtest.[/p][p][/p][h3]Visit the Oceaneers Steam page and click the "Request Access" button![/h3][h3]

notes.title: Dev Diary #5 - Tech & Research
notes.content:
[b]Oceaneers is getting closer to releasing a demo! [/b] Private playtests have been amazing, with a very positive response, and fantastic feedback. Recently with the help of this feedback we have made some tweaks to our research tree.

The latest version of the research tree has 9 categories, and within each category there are branching items, as well as improvements that unlock upgrades.

When designing a research tree, it becomes a careful balance of choosing how linear you want it to be. Linear research trees take away most decision making and are easier to use when you first play a game, but they limit choices, limit your ability to react to challenges, and limit general replayability. 

[b]When designing the research tree in Oceaneers, one of our main goals is to ensure it's not too linear - we want players to have real choices. [/b]

Perhaps you focus on establishing a solid water supply first while surviving on mediocre meals - or maybe you rush to higher tier scout boats and focus more on expeditions and scavenging.

Here is screenshot of the latest cooking section of the research tree.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45215726/2d4bec4a9b2f32a708dbcbacdc0988c551d331b4.jpg[/img]

Here is a sneak peak of the scale of the current research tree. Note that this is a work in progress and is missing a bunch of items that we are still working on.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45215726/8d69b247ad4d4aeed37f0b20ec9e45c08d92ae0e.jpg[/img]

[h2]Blueprints[/h2]
Another unique aspect of our research tree is "blueprints". There is a whole section dedicated to these blueprints, which you must find on expeditions (and when exploring bunkers). You will find some weird and wacky buildings from the old Float-Tech Corporation, and be rewarded for exploring!
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45215726/49e9ea745d02cc04c0d43543595140a5b7dcc816.jpg[/img]



That wraps up this dev diary, we would love to hear your thoughts!

notes.title: Dev Diary #4 - Survivor Stories
notes.content:
Replayabilty is a big aspect of this game genre, and we have been exploring interesting ways we can add replayability to the game. 

[h2]Introducing "Survivor Stories" [/h2]
When you start a new game, before you create your characters - you can choose your "Survivor Story". 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45215726/513fb8d784103e4f3494faece941ef73636c2806.jpg[/img]

This is the story of your group of survivors, and it determines what resources you start with, the starting stats of the group (e.g. maybe they are all starving), and any conditions you start with.

There's a lot we can with this system to create unique starting situations, and it can also impact the difficulty of the game. (E.g. an easier playthrough where the start of the game is all sunshine and coconuts - literally).

... or perhaps one of your survivors lost a fight with a shark and is in dire need of medical attention...

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45215726/e9ee9d9f882e9a7e463cab49f74f75a3ce8c002e.jpg[/img]


Survivor Stories also determine the number of survivors you start with, which can drastically change how you approach the start of the game. Perhaps more mouths to feed? Or less hands that can work!

These are only a couple of examples - we are looking forward to coming up with some interesting and quirky things in the system.

That wraps up this dev diary, we would love to hear your thoughts!

notes.title: Dev Diary #3 - Character Creator and the Magnificent Beardstache
notes.content:
Character development is integral to Oceaneers, so wouldn't it be nice if you could customize the look of your characters? Well, you can!
[list]
[*]Name your characters
[*]Customize the design
[*]Choose a background
[*]Choose starting traits
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45215726/2264455eda515698ff9d02c15895e5039cdc52de.jpg[/img]

Playtesters have already been loving huge amount of customization for characters! You can really create unique designs, making the characters your own.
[list]
[*] 40 hair styles
[*] Beards, Moustaches & Eyebrows
[*] Colors (hair, skin etc).
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45215726/95db15afe3dd19b1c40b19bb50cad2498a751804.jpg[/img]

[h2]The "Beardstache" System[/h2]
Our unique "Beardstache" system allows you to choose a separate beard and moustache, combining them together. This results in a huge amount of variety, allowing you to come up with great character designs, with facial hair in all the right places!
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45215726/0fda6cfd7f8017ffc334c2d263fc67a9469cbfb5.jpg[/img]

[h2]Backgrounds[/h2]
Character backgrounds determine their starting stats, skills they like/dislike, and in some cases give them unique traits!
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45215726/dfaf0eec3f8f6262f72c4233cd002c9b1244caae.jpg[/img]


[h2]Traits[/h2]
Choose traits to customize your characters even more. Optionally choose a bonus positive trait by taking a negative one for a little risk and reward.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45215726/b223995ee95940a0e42c89e7726d8f4a581943b3.jpg[/img]

All of these systems together allow you to create different characters when starting each playthrough. Whatever happens after that is up to the sharks!

That wraps up this dev diary, we would love to hear your thoughts!

notes.title: Dev Diary #2 - Will There Be Story & Objectives?
notes.content:
A common question we are asked is "will there be objectives/story", and we see this pop up quite a bit when players are discussing just about any crafty-buildy, survival type game (which are inherently sandbox in nature).

As gamers ourselves, we do love sandbox games, but we also [b]love progression[/b] and [b]having goals[/b] to work towards. It's one thing to set your own goals, but having core objectives and a story arc can add a lot to the game experience and was always something we wanted to have.

[b](By the way, in case you missed it, we are starting playtests soon which you can sign up for!)[/b]
https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/3052510/view/505069374726471759

For Oceaneers, the big question from a design standpoint was:
[h3]What is a compelling way to have a story gel into what is ultimately a sandbox genre, without getting in the way of the things players love about survival crafting and colony sims? [/h3]

We took inspiration from some our of favorite games such as Subnautica and No Mans Sky - which are both sandbox survival games, yet incorporate a story and objectives. We are also avid fans of old adventure games like Monkey Island and Space Quest so there are concepts from that genre that we are experimenting with as well (while taking care that they only add to the colony sim formula).

[b]Players are going to be pleasantly surprised with some of the unexpected features we are adding for story & lore (this is all new stuff that hasn't been in any trailers/screenshots yet).[/b]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45215726/acf351336e19f42aeba31dc72089c5a2d33ea2f9.jpg[/img]

We are experimenting with a range of features and techniques to get story & objectives into the game. 
[list]
[*]A core story arc/main objective.
[*]Sub-story arcs, with multiple outcomes,
[*]Optional lore to be discovered.
[*]Mini-random events that require player choice and effect your survivors (or your whole colony).
[*]Dialog between your characters for some parts of the story.
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45215726/11e47dd363a600dd19f116ec5434ba59db727554.jpg[/img]

Being a sandbox game, replayability is also important. Here are some things we are experimenting with on top of key story arcs and objectives:
[list]
[*]Starting condition choices.
[*]Starting survivor group choices.
[*]Random events.
[*]Procedural generation.
[*]Creative mode / Story-off mode.
[/list]

We are having a lot of fun testing this out, and based on feedback from initial playtests with external testers. they are loving how story and objectives are being integrated so far.

That's it for this dev diary. We would love to hear how you feel about story and objectives in games that are sandbox in nature! Do you like setting your own goals, or having a story to play through?

notes.title: Dev Diary #1 - Progress Update
notes.content:
[h1]Happy 2025! [/h1]

[b]It's finally time to start sharing more detailed ins and outs of the game features and start discussing them with you![/b]

We will be doing this in a dev blog format right here on Steam. Some entries will be general updates, but we will often focus on a specific topic for each one.

[h2]Development[/h2]
We have been working towards a demo and public playtests and will be sharing more regular updates. Internal testing has gone through several rounds and we are keen to get the community involved to gather feedback!

[h2]Features[/h2]
There are a bunch of new features we have been working on that haven’t been revealed yet (and don’t appear in the trailer or screenshots). We are finalizing a few things before we share them, stay tuned, there is some really fun depth that might surprise you!

[h2]Meanwhile... existing features we have been working on[/h2]
[b]Character stats changes.[/b]
We have been adjusting the needs, skills and conditions systems. We also have traits planned that work with these as part of the character creator. Here is an in-progress screenshot of the latest character sheet. (We will go into some detail on these systems in one of the next dev diaries).

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45215726/48d986678ff5826f9b9c6b23555fc63dbe6e1612.jpg[/img]

[b]Island inspection.[/b]
We are really excited about how island features will effect your colony and how this will tie into story and objectives. It’s going to be fun to go island hunting to find the best islands for your colony, upgrade them and add modules.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45215726/ef62c3e12715596320de9d6fe316a05ef649e264.jpg[/img]

[b]Raft building[/b]
We have been working on the raft building UI and it now features a parts list. You place everything on the raft in the dock, then the raft goes into construction and your survivors get to work. Still a work in progress, but we are happy with the direction this is going.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45215726/8808be73c3a9597435125b176a8a41d95210e614.jpg[/img]

[b]Expeditions.[/b]
The cargo system is now implemented, along with travel requirements (food/water). Resources are easy to use in the sector you are in (without inventory tetris), however, progressing to bigger and better rafts is going to be important with the cargo system to get those resources home.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45215726/10e0f935534c4669890fc7449c7f21ab61e540e2.jpg[/img]


[h2]PLAYTEST[/h2]
We are very close to playtests, if you are interested in early playtesting please join our discord. We will be doing several very small playtests before expanding it, so don’t worry if you miss out on a playtest round you will get a chance to provide feedback.

[h2]More to come![/h2]
Stay tuned, more dev diaries are on the way! We plan to go into more details on the story, character stats and resource systems, along with some other things we have been working on.


That wraps up this dev diary, we would love to hear your thoughts!

notes.title: Announcing Oceaneers, a new survival management game set on floating islands!
notes.content:
[previewyoutube=JraX1YxCPyQ;full][/previewyoutube]

[h1]We are excited to announce our new project![/h1]
[h3]A thrilling venture into the survival crafting genre set on tiny engineered islands floating in an endless ocean.[/h3]

[h2]Oh yeah.. those islands... they can sink.[/h2]

At it's core this is a shelter-survival game, you scavenge, craft and survive as you manage a small group of survivors. If you have played games like Sheltered or This War of Mine, this should be some famiilar territory for you, however your shelter isn't an underground bunker or a ruined house, it's a collection of small floating islands set on the relentless sea. If your a fan of games like Raft, Don't Starve or even Subnautica, be sure to check our [url=https://steamcommunity.com/app/3052510/discussions/0/4844274022649100133/]FAQ on the forum[/url] which includes some comparisons to some other games where we aim to be clear on exactly what this game is and isn't.

In addition to the survival mechanics you expect, you will be designing and crafting your own rafts to take on expeditions, managing island buoyancy with flotation contraptions, and hauling new islands back to your main colony to expand. You even get to progress through a story plot which revolves around the pre-flood corporation that engineered the floating islands.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

If this sounds like your type of game you can sign up for the Beta program to be notified of playtests.

[url=https://www.oceaneersgame.com/]Sign Up Here[/url]

[url=https://discord.gg/4Xz6qNpwH5]Join Discord Here[/url]

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

We have some seriously interesting features that we are yet to announce, so stay tuned as we post updates throughout development and be sure to wishlist the game.

Cheers,
